decisive_items: an abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery
The third portion of the duodenum was not seen in its expected location
an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, with small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
response.rationale: R5 is favored because the CT shows pathognomonic malrotation findings: SMA/SMV inversion, abnormal third-portion duodenum position, and low transverse colon/right colic flexure with right-sided small-bowel clustering. R2 (volvulus) is a plausible complication but lacks these malrotation-specific anatomic features and is less explanatory. The other candidates are contradicted by a normal appendix, absent surgical history, and no inflammatory bowel pattern.

rejected.why: No chronic inflammatory bowel features; imaging shows malrotation rather than bowel wall inflammation or skip lesions.
The appendix appeared normal on CT, and the RLQ tenderness and leukocytosis are nonspecific given the malrotation/volvulus pattern.
No history of abdominal surgery and no hernia sac/closed-loop; the SMA/SMV inversion and duodenal position are characteristic of malrotation, not internal hernia.
